title: POC Timeline & Milestones - Orion Tech
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood inference for Orion's conversational search + summarization workload. Agreed success criteria (latency, cost, recall/ROUGE), environment access and data subsets, benchmark plan, and milestones: kickoff, access setup, mid-point benchmark, exec readout. Action items assigned and tentative timeline set.
topics: benchmark methodology and metrics (p99/p50 latency, tokens/sec, recall/ROUGE)
access and security (VPC peering, KMS, SOC2)
timeline and milestones (kickoff, access, mid-review, exec readout)
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining today, we're gonna run through the POC timeline and make sure we have success criteria and who does what. 00:12 Samir Patel: Thanks Maya. We have Lina and Rajiv and Ava on the line. We're excited, we've been evaluating several options, want to validate latency and quality at scale. 00:24 Diego Alvarez: Hi all, Diego from Redwood SE. Quick intro — I'll own the benchmark setup and run the mid-point checks with you. 00:32 Ava Thompson: Quick note, our execs want a crisp readout — ideally we show cost delta vs our current hosted provider and a perf regression chart. 00:45 Maya Chen: Perfect, that's in scope. First, success criteria — Lina, what are your target numbers? 00:52 Lina Gomez: For our conversational search flow, p50 latency under 200ms is a stretch but ideal, p95 under 600ms. Throughput target is about 50 requests/sec for the pilot dataset. For quality, we measure recall on retrieval plus ROUGE for summarization; we want >=95% of current baseline for recall and within 0.03 ROUGE delta. 01:18 Diego Alvarez: That sounds achievable — we'll test both hosted Redwood models and a dedicated quantized variant. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token throughput. Note that p99 can spike with cold kv-cache — we'll include warmup runs. 01:36 Rajiv Menon: Security is key: VPC peering and KMS for key management, audit logs retained for 90 days, SSO via SAML. We need to see SOC2 docs. 01:50 Maya Chen: We'll share SOC2 and the security pack today. For VPC we'll need an IP range and an engineer to coordinate. 01:58 Samir Patel: Timeline — can we do a 6-week POC? Kickoff next week, access and dataset slice setup week 1-2, run benchmarks week 3-4, mid-point review at week 4, optimizations week 5, exec readout week 6. 02:14 Maya Chen: That aligns with our standard flow. Diego, you'll run the bench infra? 02:19 Diego Alvarez: Yes. I'll provision a test harness that can replay request traces and run 2 variants: hosted API and dedicated small GPU (A10-ish) with int8 quant. We'll measure latency distributions and cost-per-1000-tokens approximation. 02:36 Lina Gomez: For dataset — we can provide a 10k chat log sample plus 1k heavy summarization requests. We'll also give a golden set for quality checks. 02:46 Diego Alvarez: Good. We'll use the golden set for automated evals and store outputs. Expect some transcription mismatches in names, do we have any vendor constraints? 02:56 Samir Patel: We're evaluating Redwood and CloudX; CloudX has a managed endpoint but we've seen cost creep. Competitors are CloudX and ByteServe. 03:08 Maya Chen: Noted — we'll include a side-by-side with CloudX where comparable. 03:12 Ava Thompson: On acceptance criteria: Executive wants two clear charts — cost per 1M tokens and end-to-end latency for our two SLA tiers. Also security signoff. 03:24 Rajiv Menon: On KMS — we need to confirm customer-managed keys are supported for dedicated; if hosted, we need SSE + key rotation policy. 03:34 Diego Alvarez: We have dedicated with customer KMS in private deployments; hosted supports customer-managed keys through an HSM integration for enterprise — we'll document the options. 03:44 Maya Chen: Ok action items: we'll send the security pack, price estimate, and a bench script. 03:50 Lina Gomez: For benchmarks, define warm start vs cold start runs. 03:55 Diego Alvarez: Absolutely; we'll run 3 cold runs and 5 warm runs and report median. We'll capture KV warm ratio. 04:04 Samir Patel: Who owns staging access? 04:07 Maya Chen: Redwood will own the initial endpoint and provide creds; Orion to provide network contacts for VPC peering. 04:13 Ava Thompson: What about data retention? We need logs for 90 days and raw payloads shouldn't be used to train models. 04:20 Maya Chen: Redwood has a policy for not using customer data for training; we'll provide the data handling attestation. 04:27 Rajiv Menon: Please add RBAC for token scope and audit trail. 04:31 Diego Alvarez: That's standard — we'll enable scoped API keys for the POC and show audit logs. 04:36 Maya Chen: Mid-point review — propose week 4 with a live demo of benchmark runner and initial optimizations. 04:42 Lina Gomez: Sounds good. If results look good at mid-point, we want a canary rollout plan and a docs checklist for productionization. 04:51 Maya Chen: We'll provide a production checklist: model pinning, rollback, autoscale settings, and cost caps. 04:59 Ava Thompson: Exec readout format — 20 minute exec summary, 10 minute Q&A. 05:05 Maya Chen: Great. Any other risks? 05:08 Rajiv Menon: Network egress costs might skew cost calc, call them out. 05:12 Diego Alvarez: We'll normalize costs to token-only and call out egress separately. 05:18 Samir Patel: Ok let's recap next steps and owners. 05:22 Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send security pack, bench harness, pricing, and kickoff calendar invite. Orion to provide sample dataset, network contact, and stakeholder list. Mid-point review scheduled week 4; exec readout week 6. 05:38 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a Loom and the docs. 05:44 Meeting end.
